Job gains have been solid and unemployment remains low, reinforcing maximum employment and helping stabilize private balance sheets via reduced external finance premia (Bernanke and Gertler). Yet with sticky prices and a flat New Keynesian Phillips curve keeping inflation below 2 percent despite tight labor markets (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Nakamura and Steinsson; Galí), and with business fixed investment soft and sensitive to financing conditions, the 25 bp cut to a 2–2.25% funds-rate range fits a Taylor-rule-style, risk-management response that leans against downside risks while expectations stay anchored (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Goodfriend).
